findings.claim: Micron shares fell 11.0% to $560.85 in morning trading on November 25, 2026 after BNP Paribas Exane downgraded the stock to Neutral from Outperform and cut its price target to $775 from $1,700, saying DRAM and NAND supply and demand could balance as early as mid-2027.
findings.source_title: Why is Micron Technology stock tumbling today?

findings.claim: The same report says Goldman Sachs cut its 2028 conventional DRAM and NAND average selling price forecasts by about 20% and TrendForce lowered its 2027 DRAM contract price increase forecast on weaker consumer demand and lower server orders from Chinese cloud providers.
findings.source_title: Why is Micron Technology stock tumbling today?

findings.claim: At the TomorrowX Summit on November 18, 2026, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said 75% of Micron's 2027 output is sold out, that it is discussing 2028 commitments with customers, and that Micron has signed 26 supply and collaboration agreements with $32 billion of upfront cash and financial commitments, many running five years or longer.
findings.source_title: Micron at TomorrowX Summit: AI memory demand reshapes outlook

findings.claim: TrendForce's November 18, 2026 outlook sees conventional DRAM contract prices up 5-10% in the first quarter of 2027 and 3-8% in the second, then flat to up 5% per quarter, while it expects NAND contract prices to start falling in the first quarter of 2027.
findings.source_title: Micron's President Says Memory Has Been Tight Across Really Multiple Years. TrendForce Sees DRAM Prices Rising Through 2027

findings.claim: Fortune, as reported by Yahoo Finance, said the price ceiling in Micron's strategic customer agreements sits roughly at second-quarter 2026 DRAM prices, so output sold under those contracts does not benefit if prices rise further in 2027.
findings.source_title: Micron CEO's Nvidia message comes with warning for 2027

findings.claim: For fiscal 2026, ended September 3, 2026, Micron reported revenue of $133.188 billion versus $37.378 billion in fiscal 2025, GAAP net income of $84.969 billion, or $74.33 per diluted share, and fourth-quarter revenue of $54.229 billion with a GAAP gross margin of 86.8%.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: Micron guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion, non-GAAP gross margin to about 86.25%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $38.15 plus or minus $1.00.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: Fiscal 2026 DRAM revenue was $100.68 billion and NAND revenue was $31.79 billion, compared with $28.58 billion and $8.50 billion in fiscal 2025.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: In fiscal 2026 HBM3E 12-high was the majority of HBM shipments, Micron began volume production of HBM4 36GB 12-high and sampled HBM4 48GB 16-high, and it expects HBM4E volume to ramp in calendar 2027.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: In the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 Micron entered take-or-pay strategic customer agreements with multi-year volume commitments and price bands, and it said gross margins on those agreements should stay meaningfully above prior-cycle peak margins even at floor prices.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron received $12.75 billion of customer cash deposits in fiscal 2026 that are returned if purchase commitments are met and are mostly scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: No single customer was 10% or more of fiscal 2026 revenue, but about half of revenue came from the top ten customers and about 60% came from the data center end market.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Cash and marketable investments were $73.45 billion at September 3, 2026, versus $11.94 billion a year earlier, while debt carrying value was $5.18 billion and $2.00 billion remained undrawn on the revolving credit facility.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron estimates net capital spending of about $11.5 billion in fiscal first-quarter 2027 and about $25 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027, with spending higher in the second half.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Revenue from customers headquartered in mainland China was $8.338 billion and in Hong Kong $6.289 billion in fiscal 2026, and the 10-K says the May 2023 Cyberspace Administration of China purchasing ban on Micron products continues to affect that revenue.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron names Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk, CXMT and YMTC as competitors and says Chinese state support for domestic memory makers, plus industry capacity adds, could produce oversupply and lower average selling prices.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Long-lived assets in Taiwan were $27.613 billion at September 3, 2026, the largest geographic balance, ahead of $14.463 billion in the United States and $12.345 billion in Singapore.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron's CHIPS Act direct-funding agreements provide up to $6.1 billion for planned fabs in Boise, Idaho and Clay, New York, plus up to $275 million for Manassas, Virginia, for total grants of up to $6.4 billion, alongside a 35% investment tax credit.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: The 10-K says memory average selling prices could fall materially if demand does not keep up with new fab capacity, and that China has restricted exports of certain rare-earth materials that Micron's suppliers need.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings call, against guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion of revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00.
Customer commitments for 2028 supply, which management said are under discussion with 75% of 2027 already sold out.
First DRAM wafer output at the Boise fab, projected for mid-calendar 2027, and initial product shipments from the acquired Tongluo, Taiwan fab beginning mid-calendar 2027.
HBM advanced-packaging capacity in Singapore expected to begin expanding in early calendar 2027.

policy_links.policy: CHIPS and Science Act direct funding and the 35% advanced-manufacturing investment tax credit
policy_links.bottleneck: U.S. leading-edge memory wafer and packaging capacity
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The agreements reimburse or credit qualified U.S. fab investment, up to $6.4 billion of grants plus a 35% tax credit. They are not product purchase orders.

policy_links.policy: May 2023 Cyberspace Administration of China decision that critical information infrastructure operators may not purchase Micron products
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The 10-K says the decision reduced Micron's ability to sell to customers headquartered in mainland China and Hong Kong. Fiscal 2026 still reports $8.338 billion of revenue from mainland-China-headquartered customers and $6.289 billion from Hong Kong-headquartered customers.

key_risks.risk: Sell-side and industry forecasters are pulling forward the end of the shortage: BNP Paribas Exane sees DRAM and NAND balance by mid-2027, Goldman cut 2028 DRAM and NAND price forecasts about 20%, and TrendForce expects NAND contract prices to fall from the first quarter of 2027.
Gross margin reached 86.8% in fiscal Q4 2026. The 10-K warns that new industry capacity, including state-supported Chinese supply, can push DRAM and NAND into oversupply and cut prices materially.
About 60% of fiscal 2026 revenue was data-center demand and about half came from ten customers, so a pause in AI data-center buildout would hit the business that produced the year's results.
The largest block of long-lived assets, $27.613 billion, is in Taiwan, so a disruption there would hit manufacturing that is not duplicated elsewhere.
The CAC purchasing ban, possible further China action and China's rare-earth export restrictions can reduce sales or constrain materials.

Price ceilings in long-term agreements, reported at about second-quarter 2026 DRAM levels, cap upside on contracted volume, while $12.75 billion of customer deposits must be repaid from 2029 to 2031 and fiscal 2027 capex steps up to about $25 billion in the first half.

notes: New since November 12: Micron's November 19 release confirms the fiscal Q1 2027 call on December 17, 2026 (earlier third-party calendars said December 16); the November 18 TomorrowX Summit comments (75% of 2027 sold out, 26 agreements with $32 billion of upfront commitments); and the November 25 BNP Paribas Exane downgrade plus Goldman and TrendForce forecast cuts. The TomorrowX figures come from an Investing.com transcript summary, not a Micron filing. The Investing.com stock-move articles say they were AI-assisted and editor-reviewed. The Fortune price-ceiling detail is second-hand via Yahoo Finance, and that page shows no date. No public equity offering, ATM or convertible issuance was found; the fiscal 2026 financing section shows $10.04 billion of debt repayment, a $650 million buyback and $610 million of dividends. PwC said internal control over financial reporting was effective at September 3, 2026. CHIPS funding is grants and a tax credit, not product revenue.
